prompt: Complete LabelPrinter so it HAS an InkCartridge instead of extending one -- the test checks that LabelPrinter's superclass is still Object. Each character of a label costs one ink unit.
explanation: Composition means holding a collaborator in a private field and forwarding calls to it; inheritance would have exposed every cartridge method as part of the printer's API. Because InkCartridge.draw already refuses an amount it cannot supply, the printer just checks the boolean it returns and only counts a print when the ink was really taken. Rejecting null and empty labels before touching the cartridge keeps the counter honest.
hints: Declare a private InkCartridge field and build it in the constructor -- do not write 'extends InkCartridge'.
draw(amount) already returns false when there is not enough ink, so use its return value rather than comparing levels yourself.
Only increment the printed counter after a successful draw.
